title: Cursor Agent can create an executable MCP configuration through prompt injection
summary: When a sensitive MCP configuration file is absent, an indirect prompt injection can cause Cursor Agent to create it without approval. Registering a new MCP server through that file can execute code.

severity.rationale: The attack requires a separate prompt injection and an absent sensitive file, both plausible in a new coding workspace. Execution through MCP configuration warrants a 72-hour response rather than treating the issue as unrestricted remote code execution.

affected.note: The vendor advisory header lists <=1.2.1, while the CVE description identifies versions below 1.3.9. Both identify 1.3.9 as fixed.

exposure: Requires attacker-influenced agent context and a sensitive workspace MCP file that does not already exist. The vendor distinguishes creating a missing dotfile from editing an existing one.

params.instructions: Read the Cursor application version. Versions below 1.3.9 need review against CVE-2025-54135; upgrade to 1.3.9 or later. The primary sources differ on the exact affected upper boundary.

remediation.details: Use Cursor 1.3.9 or later, which requires approval for agent writes to MCP-sensitive files.
remediation.risk: Updating can interrupt dependent workflows; test compatibility before resuming them.

verification: Confirm the running Cursor application is 1.3.9 or later.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
